claim: Many voltage-gated potassium (Kv) channels display a time-dependent phenomenon called C-type inactivation, whereby prolonged activation by voltage leads to the inhibition of ionic conduction.
source: Many voltage-gated potassium (Kv) channels display a time-dependent phenomenon called C-type inactivation, whereby prolonged activation by voltage leads to the inhibition of ionic conduction, a process that involves a conformational change at the selectivity filter toward a non-conductive state.
evidence: This is a well-established phenomenon in the field, supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: C-type inactivation involves a conformational change at the selectivity filter toward a non-conductive state.
source: Many voltage-gated potassium (Kv) channels display a time-dependent phenomenon called C-type inactivation, whereby prolonged activation by voltage leads to the inhibition of ionic conduction, a process that involves a conformational change at the selectivity filter toward a non-conductive state.
evidence: This is established knowledge about C-type inactivation mechanism.

claim: A high-resolution structure of a strongly inactivated triple-mutant channel kv1.2-kv2.1-3m revealed a novel conformation of the selectivity filter that is dilated at its outer end.
source: Recently, a high-resolution structure of a strongly inactivated triple-mutant channel kv1.2-kv2.1-3m revealed a novel conformation of the selectivity filter that is dilated at its outer end, distinct from the well-characterized conductive state.
evidence: References a structural study (Reddi et al., 2022) that resolved this structure.

claim: The dilated filter of kv1.2-kv2.1-3m is conductive.
source: While the experimental structure was interpreted as the elusive non-conductive state, our molecular dynamics simulations and electrophysiological measurements show that the dilated filter of kv1.2-kv2.1-3m is conductive and, as such, cannot completely account for the inactivation of the channel observed in the structural experiments.
evidence: Supported by MD simulations and electrophysiological experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: An additional conformational change, implicating isoleucine residues at position 398 along the pore lining segment S6, is required to effectively block ion conduction.
source: The simulation shows that an additional conformational change, implicating isoleucine residues at position 398 along the pore lining segment S6, is required to effectively block ion conduction.
evidence: Derived from MD simulation results presented in the manuscript.

claim: The I398 residues from the four subunits act as a state-dependent hydrophobic gate located immediately beneath the selectivity filter.
source: The I398 residues from the four subunits act as a state-dependent hydrophobic gate located immediately beneath the selectivity filter.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from MD simulations showing gate closure.

claim: Ion permeation can be resumed in the kv1.2-kv2.1-3m channel when I398 is mutated to an asparagine.
source: These observations are corroborated by electrophysiological experiments showing that ion permeation can be resumed in the kv1.2-kv2.1-3m channel when I398 is mutated to an asparagine—a mutation that does not abolish C-type inactivation since digitoxin (AgTxII) fails to block the ionic permeation of kv1.2-kv2.1-3m_I398N.
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological measurements presented in Figure 3.

claim: The I398N mutation does not abolish C-type inactivation since AgTxII fails to block the ionic permeation of kv1.2-kv2.1-3m_I398N.
source: These observations are corroborated by electrophysiological experiments showing that ion permeation can be resumed in the kv1.2-kv2.1-3m channel when I398 is mutated to an asparagine—a mutation that does not abolish C-type inactivation since digitoxin (AgTxII) fails to block the ionic permeation of kv1.2-kv2.1-3m_I398N.
evidence: Supported by toxin blocking experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: The selectivity filter of Kv channels can exist in both conductive and non-conductive states.
source: It is well established that the selectivity filter of Kv channels can exist in both conductive and non-conductive states (Figure 1).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: C-type inactivation contributes to fine-tune long-term activity of Kv channels.
source: Known as the process of (slow) C-type inactivation (Hoshi et al., 1990; Ostmeyer et al., 2013), the conductive to non-conductive conformational transition is of great physiological importance as it contributes to fine-tune long-term activity of Kv channels.
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work (Hoshi et al., 1990; Ostmeyer et al., 2013).

claim: The canonical conductive conformational state of the filter was first revealed with the crystallographic structure of the prototypical bacterial K+ channel KcsA at high resolution.
source: The canonical conductive conformational state of the filter was first revealed with the crystallographic structure of the prototypical bacterial K+ channel KcsA at high resolution (e.g. PDB id 1BL8 [Doyle et al., 1998] or 1K4C [Zhou et al., 2001]).
evidence: References specific PDB structures from cited studies.

claim: Molecular dynamics studies confirm that ion conduction along the conductive filter conformation is possible and unopposed by large free-energy barriers.
source: Molecular dynamics (MD) studies confirm that ion conduction along this filter conformation is possible and unopposed by large free-energy barriers (Bernèche and Roux, 2001; Kopec et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous MD studies.

claim: High-resolution structures of Kv channels revealed a novel conformation of the selectivity filter that is partially dilated at its outer end and constricted near its internal face.
source: Recently, high-resolution structures of Kv channels revealed a novel conformation of the selectivity filter that is partially dilated at its outer end and constricted near its internal face (Tan et al., 2022; Reddi et al., 2022; Yangyu et al., 2024).
evidence: References multiple structural studies.

claim: The 'dilated' conformation has been interpreted as the non-conductive conformational state of the selectivity filter, accounting for the phenomenon of C-type inactivation.
source: Because a number of mutations known to strongly enhance the process of C-type inactivation were introduced in the construct used in structural determination (Perozo et al., 1993), this 'dilated' conformation has been interpreted as the non-conductive conformational state of the selectivity filter, accounting for the phenomenon of C-type inactivation.
evidence: This is the interpretation from previous structural studies that the current manuscript challenges.

claim: The most recent structure of the wild-type Shaker B channel displays the same dilated conformation of the filter at low concentration of external potassium.
source: Reinforcing that notion, the most recent structure of the wild-type Shaker B channel displays the same dilated conformation of the filter at low concentration of external potassium (Stix et al., 2023).
evidence: References a recent structural study.

claim: The all-atom root-mean-square deviations (RMSD) of the selectivity filter between the dilated and the conductive conformation is about 3.0 Å.
source: The all-atom root-mean-square deviations (RMSD) of the selectivity filter between the dilated and the conductive conformation is about 3.0 Å, arising mostly from rearrangements of the side chain of the highly conserved tyrosine and aspartic acid along the signature of the selectivity filter TVGYGD (Figure 1).
evidence: Structural comparison shown in Figure 1.

claim: The selectivity filter in the dilated conformation is accessible to the intracellular solution via a large open and hydrated vestibular cavity.
source: The selectivity filter in the dilated conformation is accessible to the intracellular solution via a large open and hydrated vestibular cavity.
evidence: Structural observation from the dilated conformation structure.

claim: The voltage drop across the selectivity filter through the conductive and dilated conformations is similar.
source: Besides, the voltage drop across the selectivity filter through the conductive and dilated conformations is similar (Figure 1C).
evidence: Computational analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The kv1.2-kv2.1-3m channel with the dilated selectivity filter appears remarkably stable during a 10 μs simulation using the AMBER force field.
source: The kv1.2-kv2.1-3m channel with the dilated selectivity filter appears remarkably stable during a 10 μs simulation using the AMBER force field (Figure 2).
evidence: MD simulation results shown in Figure 2.

claim: The structural RMSD of the selectivity filter relative to the initial X-ray structure is less than 2.8 Å in AMBER simulations.
source: The structural RMSD of the selectivity filter relative to the initial X-ray structure (Reddi et al., 2022) is less than 2.8 Å, indicative of structural stability (Figure 2B, structural deviation R).
evidence: MD simulation analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: There is an early voltage-driven K+ conduction event across the selectivity filter within the first ~2 μs of the AMBER simulation.
source: According to a hard-knock mechanism at the level of binding sites S4 and S3 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1; Stix et al., 2023), there is an early voltage-driven K+ conduction event across the selectivity filter within the first ~2 μs of the simulation (Figure 2B, trajectory of K+ along the permeation pathway Z).
evidence: MD simulation results shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ion access to the central cavity of the channel and their subsequent conduction across the selectivity filter completely cease after ~4 μs of simulation time when the side chain of isoleucine at position 398 from all four S6 segments twist toward the central axis of the channel.
source: More specifically, ion access to the central cavity of the channel and their subsequent conduction across the selectivity filter completely cease after ~4 μs of simulation time when the side chain of isoleucine at position 398 from all four S6 segments twist toward the central axis of the channel, dehydrating and blocking the permeation pathway immediately beneath the selectivity filter (Figure 2B, density of water along the pore axis).
evidence: MD simulation results shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The Cβ-Cβ distance between I398 in opposing subunits decreases over a period of 3–4 μs, reaching a value of about 9 Å.
source: The Cβ-Cβ distance between I398 in opposing subunits decreases over a period of 3–4 μs, reaching a value of about 9 Å—in stark contrast with the initial distance of 15 Å in the X-ray structure (Reddi et al., 2022; Figure 2, separation distance L of I398).
evidence: MD simulation analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: Ion conduction events are observed in the simulation with the CHARMM36m force field.
source: In contrast, ion conduction events are observed in the simulation with the CHARMM36m force field.
evidence: MD simulation results with CHARMM36m force field.

claim: The CHARMM36m force field favors the open configuration of the isoleucine gate.
source: Because the CHARMM36m force field favors the open configuration of the isoleucine gate, the simulation shows that the dilated conformation is highly conductive under membrane depolarization.
evidence: Inference from MD simulation behavior with CHARMM36m.

claim: The dilated conformation is highly conductive under membrane depolarization when the isoleucine gate is open.
source: Because the CHARMM36m force field favors the open configuration of the isoleucine gate, the simulation shows that the dilated conformation is highly conductive under membrane depolarization.
evidence: MD simulation results with CHARMM36m force field.

claim: The dilated conformation of the selectivity filter is conductive when the isoleucine gate is open.
source: Compared to the unrestrained simulation with the AMBER force field, a larger number of ions access the central cavity of the channel, triggering two spontaneous conduction events across the selectivity filter in the early ~4 μs of the simulation. The density profile of the K+ ion along the channel axis is distinct from that of the unconstrained simulation. Partial reallocation of the ionic density from sites S4/S3 to sites S2/S1 reflects the increased mobility of K+ in the selectivity filter, thereby corroborating the hypothesis that the dilated conformation of the selectivity filter is conductive when the isoleucine gate is open.
evidence: MD simulation with restraints to keep I398 gate open, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The total number of conduction events across the dilated conformation of the selectivity filter over the total simulation time is 44 (ions)/30 μs.
source: According to the voltage-driven MD trajectories in which the isoleucine gate is open, the total number of conduction events across the dilated conformation of the selectivity filter over the total simulation time is 44 (ions)/30 μs (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: Quantitative analysis of MD simulation data.

claim: The ionic current of a macroscopic population of ion channels in the open-gate dilated state is ~0.2 pA at the TM voltage of +200 mV.
source: Based on the number of crossing events per simulation time, the ionic current of a macroscopic population of ion channels in the open-gate dilated state is ~0.2 pA at the TM voltage of +200 mV (single-channel conductance of ~1.17 pS in symmetric 150 mM KCl).
evidence: Calculated from MD simulation conduction events.

claim: The estimate of ~0.2 pA is orders of magnitude larger than the measured current in the triple-mutant channel upon C-type inactivation.
source: In all likelihood underestimation of the channel conductance as a consequence of the well-documented force-field limitations in reproducing the ionic current in Kv channels at low voltages (<300 mV) (Jensen et al., 2013), the estimate of ~0.2 pA is still orders of magnitude larger than the measured current in the triple-mutant channel upon C-type inactivation (vide infra), and, therefore, the conductivity properties of the 'dilated' conformation of the selectivity filter cannot explain alone the inactivation of kv1.2-kv2.1-3m under membrane depolarization.
evidence: Comparison between simulation and experimental data.

claim: C-type inactivation is greatly enhanced in the triple-mutant channel kv1.2-kv2.1-3m.
source: In stark contrast with recordings of the kv1.2-kv2.1 chimera channel (Figure 3A), C-type inactivation is greatly enhanced in the triple-mutant channel kv1.2-kv2.1-3m, as is evidenced by the fast decay of the ionic current in the ms timescale and the macroscopic current appearing on similar scales as gating current (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Electrophysiological measurements shown in Figure 3.

claim: Substitution of the isoleucine by the polar amino acid asparagine restores the conductivity of the triple-mutant channel.
source: However, substitution of the isoleucine by the polar amino acid asparagine, with similar side-chain volume, restores the conductivity of the triple-mutant channel (Figure 3C).
evidence: Electrophysiological measurements shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Mutation I398N drastically increases ionic conduction without any apparent time-dependent inactivation.
source: While not disturbing the current-voltage relationship of the triple-mutant channel, mutation I398N drastically increases ionic conduction without any apparent time-dependent inactivation (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: Electrophysiological measurements shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: Restoration of ion conduction with I398N is not caused by inadvertently stabilizing the selectivity filter in the conductive state.
source: Importantly, restoration of ion conduction with I398N is not caused by inadvertently stabilizing the selectivity filter in the conductive state, as demonstrated by pore-blocking toxin assays.
evidence: Demonstrated by toxin blocking experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: Agitoxin-II (AgTxII), dendrotoxin, and charybdotoxin (CTX) are potent toxin blockers of Kv channels.
source: Agitoxin-II (AgTxII), dendrotoxin, and charybdotoxin (CTX) are potent toxin blockers of Kv channels (Takacs et al., 2009), binding to the outer mouth of the channel (Yangyu et al., 2024; Eriksson and Roux, 2002; Banerjee et al., 2013).
evidence: Established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Pore-blocking toxins preferentially bind and occlude the conductive conformation of the selectivity filter of Kv channels.
source: Such pore-blocking toxins preferentially bind and occlude the conductive conformation of the selectivity filter of Kv channels and are not effective in blocking channels that have W434F-like selectivity filter, as indicated by previous functional studies (Kitaguchi et al., 2004) as well as implicit solvent binding free-energy calculations (Materials and methods, Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 2, Supplementary file 5).
evidence: Supported by previous studies and computational calculations shown in Figure 3F.

claim: AgTxII blocks the ionic current across the conductive kv1.2-kv2.1 channel by binding to the outer mouth of the filter in the conductive conformation.
source: Whereas AgTxII blocks the ionic current across the conductive kv1.2-kv2.1 channel by binding to the outer mouth of the filter in the conductive conformation (Figure 3G), it fails to bind and occlude the kv1.2-kv2.1-3m channel with its filter mostly in the dilated conformation (Figure 3H).
evidence: Electrophysiological experiments shown in Figure 3G and H.

claim: AgTxII fails to bind and occlude the kv1.2-kv2.1-3m channel with its filter mostly in the dilated conformation.
source: Whereas AgTxII blocks the ionic current across the conductive kv1.2-kv2.1 channel by binding to the outer mouth of the filter in the conductive conformation (Figure 3G), it fails to bind and occlude the kv1.2-kv2.1-3m channel with its filter mostly in the dilated conformation (Figure 3H).
evidence: Electrophysiological experiments shown in Figure 3H.

claim: The resumed ion permeation in kv1.2-kv2.1-3m_I398N is not caused by any stabilization effect of I398N on the selectivity filter and most likely the ions are conducting through the dilated filter.
source: Similar effect is observed in Kv1.2-kv2.1-3m_I398N, suggesting the resumed ion permeation is not caused by any stabilization effect of I398N on the selectivity filter and most likely the ions are conducting through the dilated filter (Figure 3I).
evidence: Electrophysiological experiments shown in Figure 3I.

claim: The ion conduction in kv1.2-kv2.1-3m_I398N mutant indicates that the permeation pathway must be altered at some location along the permeation pathway other than the selectivity filter.
source: Because kv1.2-kv2.1-3m and kv1.2-kv2.1-3m_I398N are not affected by the toxin (Figure 3J), the ion conduction in kv1.2-kv2.1-3m_I398N mutant indicates that the permeation pathway must be altered at some location along the permeation pathway other than the selectivity filter.
evidence: Inference from toxin blocking experiments shown in Figure 3J.

claim: A double mutant (S367T/V377T) of the chimera channel kv1.2-kv2.1-2m that does not inactivate is blocked by AgTxII, irrespective of the I398N mutation.
source: Such structural modifications of the permeation pathway are specific of C-type inactivation since a double mutant (S367T/V377T) of the chimera channel kv1.2-kv2.1-2m that does not inactivate and is blocked by AgTxII, irrespective of the I398N mutation (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), suggesting that I398N mutation neither affect the selectivity filter of kv1.2-kv2.1-2m nor kv1.2-kv2.1-3m.
evidence: Electrophysiological experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The critical C-type inactivation mutation W362F is missing in the kv1.2-kv2.1-2m channel, hence its inability to slow-inactivate.
source: The critical C-type inactivation mutation W362F (Perozo et al., 1993) is missing in the kv1.2-kv2.1-2m channel, hence its inability to slow-inactivate.
evidence: Explanation of experimental observations based on known mutation effects.

claim: A polar amino acid allows ion conduction by keeping the permeation pathway constitutively hydrated and open.
source: Consistent with experiment, a polar amino acid allows ion conduction by keeping the permeation pathway constitutively hydrated and open.
evidence: Conclusion from MD simulations of I398N mutant.

claim: I398N prevents closure of the gate at position 398.
source: Additional simulations of the triple-mutant channel support this view by revealing that I398N prevents closure of the gate at position 398 (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: MD simulation results shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: The dilated conformation of the selectivity filter of kv1.2-kv2.1-3m is conductive.
source: Taken together, the present computational and experimental results demonstrate that the dilated conformation of the selectivity filter of kv1.2-kv2.1-3m is conductive and that an isoleucine gate is critical to block K+ currents during C-type inactivation of the channel.
evidence: Main conclusion from combined computational and experimental results.

claim: An isoleucine gate is critical to block K+ currents during C-type inactivation of the channel.
source: Taken together, the present computational and experimental results demonstrate that the dilated conformation of the selectivity filter of kv1.2-kv2.1-3m is conductive and that an isoleucine gate is critical to block K+ currents during C-type inactivation of the channel.
evidence: Main conclusion from combined computational and experimental results.

claim: The isoleucine gate seems to be relevant for potassium channels that undergo C-type inactivation in general.
source: Judged by the primary sequence conservation of I398 (Figure 3—figure supplement 5), the isoleucine gate seems to be relevant for potassium channels that undergo C-type inactivation in general, and, potentially, for other voltage-gated Na+ channels possessing distinct selectivity filters (Liu et al., 2023).
evidence: Inference from sequence conservation analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: The action of the isoleucine gate in C-type inactivation is averted by the I398N mutation because the pathway remains hydrated with the polar asparagine side.
source: The action of the isoleucine gate in C-type inactivation is averted by the I398N mutation because the pathway remains hydrated with the polar asparagine side.
evidence: Mechanistic explanation based on MD simulations and experiments.

claim: In the homologous Shaker B channel, the single mutation I470C affects the rate of inactivation.
source: In the homologous Shaker B channel, the single mutation I470C affects the rate of inactivation (Holmgren et al., 1997; Peters et al., 2013) while the double mutation T449V/I470C (Olcese et al., 2001) converts the slow inactivated state into a conductive state.
evidence: Supported by citations to previous experimental studies.

claim: The double mutation T449V/I470C converts the slow inactivated state into a conductive state.
source: In the homologous Shaker B channel, the single mutation I470C affects the rate of inactivation (Holmgren et al., 1997; Peters et al., 2013) while the double mutation T449V/I470C (Olcese et al., 2001) converts the slow inactivated state into a conductive state.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous experimental study.

claim: Closing of the I398 gate in the dilated conformation of kv1.2-kv2.1-3m involves occlusion of the binding site of internally applied quaternary ammonium (QA) blockers.
source: Closing of the I398 gate in the dilated conformation of kv1.2-kv2.1-3m involves occlusion of the binding site of internally applied quaternary ammonium (QA) blockers (Lenaeus et al., 2005), explaining the previously reported 20-fold decreased affinity of TEA for the inactivated state of Shaker-IR compared with that of the open state (Panyi and Deutsch, 2007).
evidence: Inference connecting current findings to previous experimental observations.

claim: The mechanism whereby I398N renders the gate constitutively open is consistent with the demonstration that I470C in Shaker-IR morphs the channel that does not trap QA blockers into one that does.
source: On the other hand, the mechanism whereby I398N renders the gate constitutively open, not occluding the binding site of QA blockers, is also consistent with the demonstration that I470C in Shaker-IR morphs the channel that does not trap QA blockers into one that does (Holmgren et al., 1997) and with the fact that MTSEA modifications on the inactivated state are sixfold slower than in the open state of the T449K/I470C Shaker-IR (Panyi and Deutsch, 2007).
evidence: Inference connecting current findings to previous experimental observations.

claim: The modus operandi of the isoleucine gate is expected to be coupled to the PVP motif.
source: Across all these measured effects, the modus operandi of the isoleucine gate is expected to be coupled to the PVP motif, and, therefore, to reflect to some extent the conformational allostery between the selectivity filter and the bundle-crossing region previously reported for C-type inactivation (Panyi and Deutsch, 2007; Cuello et al., 2017; Labro et al., 2018).
evidence: Inference based on observed coupling in simulations and previous literature.

claim: Ion conduction through the selectivity filter in the canonical 'conductive' conformation tends to be too small compared to experimental values with well-established force fields like AMBER and CHARMM36m, especially at physiological voltages.
source: Even with well-established force fields like AMBER and CHARMM36m, ion conduction through the selectivity filter in the canonical 'conductive' conformation tends to be too small compared to experimental values, especially at physiological voltages (less 50 mV) (Jensen et al., 2013).
evidence: Known limitation of force fields, supported by citation.

claim: With AMBER, there is observable ion conduction via the hard-knock mechanism but a fairly high voltage (200–300 mV) is required to generate a significant ionic current.
source: With AMBER, there is observable ion conduction via the hard-knock mechanism (no water molecules between the ions) but a fairly high voltage (200–300 mV) is required to generate a significant ionic current (Köpfer et al., 2014).
evidence: Known behavior of AMBER force field, supported by citation.

claim: With CHARMM36m, there is observable conduction via the hard-knock mechanism at high voltages, albeit less so than with AMBER.
source: With CHARMM36m, there is also observable conduction via the hard-knock mechanism at high voltages, albeit less so than with AMBER.
evidence: Observation from MD simulations in this study.

claim: There is no substantial ion conduction with the AMBER force field along the dilated conformation because the ion binds strongly to the selectivity filter sites S4 and S3.
source: Here, along the dilated conformation of the selectivity filter, we find that there is no substantial ion conduction with the AMBER force field because the ion binds strongly to the selectivity filter sites S4 and S3.
evidence: Observation from MD simulations in this study.

claim: There is noticeable ion conduction with the CHARMM36m force field because the ion does not bind strongly to the sites S4 and S3.
source: However, there is noticeable ion conduction with the CHARMM36m force field because the ion does not bind strongly to the sites S4 and S3.
evidence: Observation from MD simulations in this study.

claim: Multiple conduction events across the open-dilated conformation of the triple-mutant chimera channel were observed in the simulation with the CHARMM36m force field, with no applied restraints.
source: In fact, multiple conduction events across the open-dilated conformation of the triple-mutant chimera channel were observed in the simulation with the CHARMM36m force field, with no applied restraints.
evidence: Observation from MD simulations in this study.

claim: The structures of kv1.2-kv2.1-3m, Shaker-W434F, Kv1.2-W366F, and Shaker-lowK correspond to a conductive metastable intermediate on the path toward the true non-conductive C-type inactivated state.
source: Based on our findings, we propose that the structures of kv1.2-kv2.1-3m (Reddi et al., 2022), Shaker-W434F (Tan et al., 2022), Kv1.2-W366F (Yangyu et al., 2024), and Shaker-lowK (Stix et al., 2023) corresponds to a conductive metastable intermediate on the path toward the true non-conductive C-type inactivated state wherein the permeation pathway is blocked by the isoleucine gate.
evidence: Proposed model based on combined computational and experimental findings.

claim: The free-energy landscape associated with C-type inactivation comprises two sequential transitions between three metastable states: conductive → dilated-intermediate → deeply inactivated.
source: The free-energy landscape associated with the with C-type inactivation process comprises two sequential transitions between three metastable states: conductive → dilated-intermediate → deeply inactivated.
evidence: Proposed model based on free-energy calculations shown in Figure 4.

claim: The transition from conductive to dilated state favors the dilated state with a downhill free-energy change of –12 kcal/mol.
source: The first PMF monitoring the conformation of the selectivity filter while the isoleucine gate is in the open conformation shows two metastable states: conductive and dilated. The transition, which favors the latter state with a downhill free-energy change of –12 kcal/mol, involves a significant conformational change of Y373 from its buried configuration next to T367 in the conductive state toward its externally exposed orientation in the intermediate state resulting from unfavorable close interactions between the polar side chain of Y373 and F362.
evidence: Free-energy calculation results shown in Figure 4.

claim: The transition from dilated-intermediate to deeply inactivated state shows a downhill change of –6.0 kcal/mol.
source: As shown by the second PMF monitoring the closure of the isoleucine gate toward a non-conductive deep inactivated state while the filter remains in dilated conformation shows a downhill change of –6.0 kcal/mol.
evidence: Free-energy calculation results shown in Figure 4.

claim: At +200 mV, the time constant of C-type inactivation is predicted to be in the same microsecond range of the simulated deep inactivation of the channel.
source: Notwithstanding the limited accuracies of these computational estimates, the forward and backward free-energy barriers for these two transitions are in qualitative agreement with C-type inactivation of the triple-mutant channel in the sense that kv1.2-kv2.1-3m inactivates substantially faster than recovers from it—at +200 mV, the time constant of C-type inactivation is predicted to be in the same microsecond range of the simulated deep inactivation of the channel (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Comparison between free-energy calculations and experimental timescales shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: One or two Na+ ions can stably bind the dilated conformation of the selectivity filter at sites S3, S4, and Sext in the presence of 150 mM NaCl.
source: AMBER and CHARM36m simulations of kv1.2-kv2.1-3m in presence of 150 mM NaCl show that one or two Na+ ions can stably bind the dilated conformation of the selectivity filter at sites S3, S4, and Sext, while favoring the open configuration of the isoleucine gate (Materials and methods, Figure 4—figure supplement 3 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: MD simulation results shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: The internal [Na+]/[K+] concentration ratio seems to affect the closing of the isoleucine gate with functional implications for sodium leak in C-type inactivation.
source: The internal [Na+]/[K+] concentration ratio seems to affect the closing of the isoleucine gate with functional implications for sodium leak in C-type inactivation.
evidence: Inference from MD simulations with Na+ ions.

claim: Most studied potassium channels including Kv1.2, Shaker-B, KcsA, and MthK display either isoleucine, leucine, valine, or phenylalanine at position 398.
source: In particular, note that except for hERG, most studied potassium channels including, Kv1.2, Shaker-B, KcsA, and MthK, display either isoleucine, leucine, valine, or phenylalanine at position 398 (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Sequence analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: The hERG channel has a tyrosine at position 398 which in the cryo-EM structure is twisted toward the central cavity in the open state.
source: The hERG channel has a tyrosine at position 398 which in the cryo-EM structure (Wang and MacKinnon, 2017) is twisted toward the central cavity in the open state.
evidence: Observation from cited cryo-EM structure.

claim: C-type inactivation in hERG might also involve constriction of the permeation pathway at position 398 when the selectivity filter is dilated.
source: Because tyrosine is bulkier than asparagine, there is a chance that C-type inactivation in hERG also involves constriction of the permeation pathway at position 398 when the selectivity filter is dilated—another fascinating assumption worth of investigation in structural studies.
evidence: Speculation based on structural comparison.

claim: The isoleucine gate might interfere in a state-dependent manner with the mechanism of action of a broad class of QA blockers and negatively charged activators.
source: As a piece of the molecular machinery implicated in multiple states, the isoleucine gate might interfere in a state-dependent manner with the mechanism of action of a broad class of QA blockers (Panyi and Deutsch, 2007) and negatively charged activators that bind beneath the selectivity filter and operate as master keys to open a variety of K+ channels (Schewe et al., 2019).
evidence: Speculation about broader implications, supported by citations.

claim: The understanding of the isoleucine gate could offer a distinct advantage in the development of drugs that modulate gating states of potassium channels more specifically.
source: Of particular importance, the understanding of this last aspect could offer a distinct advantage in the development of drugs that modulate gating states of potassium channels more specifically.
evidence: Speculation about potential applications.
